verdict.rationale: Sentry's source is publicly readable: there is a public getsentry/sentry GitHub repo, users report reading the code to build integrations, and self-hosters install it via git clone. However, the evidence shows it was relicensed to the Business Source License, which some users treat as no longer open-source, so the 'open license' part is only partly met. Missing for 10: first-party license documentation, and confirmation that the current license qualifies as an open (OSI-style) license rather than source-available BSL.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: the fully open-source code helped them build advanced integrations because they could read exactly what the code does instead of relying on docs
the move to the Business Source License very disappointing
installation is git clone, editing one or two config files, and running ./install.sh
